JAAC has called on people to protest against the reservation of 12 legislative seats in the local assembly for refugees who migrated to Pakistan from Indian-administered Kashmir decades ago. The seats allocated for displaced Kashmiris date back to legislation introduced in the 1970sto ensure people from Indian-administered Kashmir - and who settled in Pakistan hoping one day to return to their homes if a long-standing dispute over the region was resolved - still had a say in the territory's governance. JAAC has called for the abolition of the reserved seats, arguing they undermine local representation and that all the seats in the legislature should be for those who actually reside in the region.

reranked_evidence.title: President, PM reaffirm support for Kashmiris' right to self-determination - The Express Tribune
reranked_evidence.snippet: The 78th Kashmir Accession Day (*Youm-e-Ilhaq-e-Pakistan)* to Pakistan was observed across the country on Sunday to commemorate the historic resolution adopted by the All Jammu and Kashmir Muslim Conference on July 19, 1947, calling for the accession of the princely state of Jammu and Kashmir to Pakistan. President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif reaffirmed Pakistan's unwavering support for the people of Jammu and Kashmir on the occasion of Kashmir’s Accession to Pakistan Day and urged the international community and the United Nations to play a more active role in ensuring the implementation of UN resolutions. reranked_evidence.title: Accession Day: Shehbaz renews commitment to Kashmiris’ right to self-determination - Hum News English
reranked_evidence.snippet: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Sunday reaffirmed Pakistan’s unwavering diplomatic, political and moral support for the people of Jammu and Kashmir, saying the country would continue to stand by their right to self-determination. In his message on the occasion of Kashmir’s Accession to Pakistan Day, the prime minister said the day commemorates the historic resolution adopted by the All Jammu and Kashmir Muslim Conference during its Srinagar session on July 19, 1947. Reaffirming Pakistan’s longstanding position, the prime minister said the country remains steadfast in its principled support for the inalienable right to self-determination of the people of Jammu and Kashmir, as enshrined in the relevant United Nations Security Council resolutions. He also paid tribute to the courage, resilience and steadfastness of the people of Indian Illegally Occupied Jammu and Kashmir (IIOJK), saying Pakistan would continue to extend unwavering diplomatic, political and moral support until they are able to exercise their inalienable right to self-determination.
